title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 97-98
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 97 to 98 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 97 to 98 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 97 to 98.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 97 to 98** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**अरौद्रः कुण्डली चक्री विक्रम्यूर्जितशासनः । शब्दातिगः शब्दसहः शिशिरः शर्वरीकरः ॥** **अक्रूरः पेशलो दक्षो दक्षिणः क्षमिणां वरः । विद्वत्तमो वीतभयः पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तनः ॥**

Not harsh, wearing earrings and the discus is he. Mighty, with a command none can resist, is that God of gods. Beyond words, hearing every word, cool and soothing, the maker of night. He is never cruel, gentle, skilful, generous and the best among those who forgive. The wisest of the wise, the fearless one, is that God of gods. Even to hear and sing his glory is a blessing.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 97 to 98 mean?
faq.a: Not harsh, wearing earrings and the discus is he. Mighty, with a command none can resist, is that God of gods. Beyond words, hearing every word, cool and soothing, the maker of night. He is never cruel, gentle, skilful, generous and the best among those who forgive. The wisest of the wise, the fearless one, is that God of gods. Even to hear and sing his glory is a blessing.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
